text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated 5xx rate and p95 latency spike for eu-west (region: eu-west1). metric: generation_errors=6.8% (baseline 0.2%), p95=1240ms (baseline 120ms). Paging on-call.

Maya: I'm on it. Seeing a surge in queued requests and a bunch of node-level OOMs. Starting diagnosis.

Eric: Any customer-facing alerts yet? SLAs impacted?

Maya: Small cohort of customers seeing failures and timeouts for heavy-context requests. Estimated impacted sessions ~4.5% of active traffic in eu-west, with error spike concentrated on long-seq jobs (seq>2048).

Sidharth: @Maya can we throttle long contexts first? Prefer a graded mitigation vs full region failover.

Maya: Yes. Plan A: apply staged traffic shaping + reduce long-context concurrency + disable expensive auxiliary features (rerank/embedding fallback) for eu-west. Plan B: if error rate doesn't drop within 12 min, shift 30% of the region traffic to us-west and 20% to apac as safety.

Juan: I'll prepare route policy changes. Will use rictl to adjust quotas and weights.

Maya: I'm going to push the following: 1) apply a per-model rate cap on seq>=2048 requests, 2) reduce per-tenant concurrency for best-effort tier, 3) toggle off reranker for non-critical routes.

Maya: Applying initial rate limit now.

Maya: ```
# apply temporary traffic policy
rictl traffic-policy apply --region eu-west1 \
  --match "seq_len>=2048" \
  --limit 10rps --burst 20 --reason "incident: long-seq throttling"
```

Maya: Policy applied. Observability: 60s after apply, error rate dropped from 6.8% -> 3.1% and queue depth fell by ~40%.

Eric: Good. Can we also reduce background batch embed jobs hitting the region?

Juan: Kicking off temporary quota change for batch embedding consumer group.

Juan: ```
rictl quota update --consumer batch-embeds --region eu-west1 --qps 0.5 --reason "incident: reduce load"
```

IncidentBot: DeployBot reports: config-change accepted by control plane, rolling to edge-proxies.

Maya: Next I want to gradually shift spillover traffic for model-gamma to us-west. Starting a canary with 10% traffic.

Sidharth: Recommend setting a max fallout window to 4m and monitoring TLS handshake errors and 5xx trend. If p95 in us-west > 500ms or 5xx increases, rollback.

Maya: Canary applied. ```rictl route weight --src eu-west1 --dst us-west1 --model model-gamma --weight 0.10``` Observing metrics.

Maya: Canary stable at 10m; us-west latency stable and eu-west errors down to 1.9%. Proceeding to 30% shift as pre-planned.

Maya: Bumping to 30% now. ```rictl route weight --src eu-west1 --dst us-west1 --model model-gamma --weight 0.30``` Will also add an automatic fallback to local variants if cross-region fails.

IncidentBot: Auto-alert: quota burn rate on provider-B (apac) climbing due to spillover. Consider provider routing cap.

Juan: Adding provider-B cap to 20% of new spill traffic. ```rictl provider cap --provider provider-B --region eu-west1 --cap 0.20``` 

Maya: Also disabling experimental feature-flag 'semantic-cache-write' for eu-west to lower write load.

Maya: ```
feature-flag toggle --flag semantic-cache-write --region eu-west1 --state off --note "incident mitigation"
```

Eric: Customer impact notice draft: "We've applied scoped throttles for long-context requests and staged traffic reroutes to reduce errors. Some high-cost requests may see higher latency or rejections temporarily. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes." Approve and send?

SupportBot: I'll post to status.redwood.ai/incidents and queue the message to impacted customers list.

Maya: Approve. Post now please.

SupportBot: Posted. Incident status page updated; customers tagged: enterprise-eu cohort (approx 82 tenants).

Sidharth: Monitoring rolling. Two checks: (1) region error rate <1% sustained for 10m, (2) provider capacity breach alarms cleared. If both hold, we'll convert to a maintenance ticket and start cleanup in 60m.

Maya: We're at 0.8% errors and p95=260ms in eu-west after the shifts. Provider-B cap holding. Queue lengths normalized.

Eric: Nice work. Any follow-ups for Dedicated customers who might need SLA credits or manual capacity bump?

SupportBot: Created follow-up ticket: SD-6842 to coordinate Dedicated bumps / credits. Assigned to Customer Success.

Maya: Start gradual rollback of feature toggles and quotas after 45m stable. I'll handoff to night on-call in the next update.

Juan: Notes for postmortem: root cause likely hot-path memory regression in model-gamma inference path triggered by large seq patterns + degraded kernel fallback on a subset of eu-west accelerators. Collecting profiler logs and kernel OOM traces.

IncidentBot: Incident update: mitigations applied, region spillover in effect, customers notified. Status: Stabilizing. Next update in 30 minutes.

Maya: Handoff to @Sidharth for next shift if still unstable. Leaving runbook entries and commands used in thread. Thanks team :heart:

Sidharth: Taking over. Will continue to monitor and start collection for postmortem artifacts. If we see re-escalation I'll re-open paging.

Maya: last_message: proceeding to cleanup plan in 45m contingent on stability.
